1. PepsiCo's beverage business actually grew volume in Q3 when excluding the case pack water divestment, with Pepsi brand growing volume, net revenue, and market share.
2. Service levels for both food and beverage businesses are now at 97%-98% following earlier systems transition issues.
3. The Away From Home channel is growing 2-3x faster than the retail business in both U.S. and internationally.
4. PepsiCo expects to return to its long-term algorithm for net revenue growth within 2026, though timing may vary between Q3 and Q4.
5. The Frito-Lay food business in North America returned to growth in the last 4 weeks of the quarter, with management expecting close to flat organic sales in Q4.
6. International business returned to mid- to high mid-single-digit performance in September after a weaker summer impacted by weather.
7. Brazil delivered close to double-digit growth in September.
8. Baja Blast has become a $1 billion retail value platform when combining PepsiCo sales and Taco Bell sales.
9. Propel has been growing at a double-digit CAGR for the last 5-6 years.
10. CFO Jamie Caulfield is retiring after 33 years with the company, and Steve from Walmart will be joining as the new CFO to help execute Strategy 2030.

1. Delta reported Q3 2025 revenue of $15.2 billion, up 4.1% year-over-year, with pretax income of $1.5 billion, earnings of $1.71 per share, and an 11.2% operating margin.
2. Free cash flow was $830 million in Q3, bringing year-to-date free cash flow to $2.8 billion, with full-year guidance updated to $3.5 billion to $4 billion.
3. Delta generated a return on invested capital of 13%, which is 5 points above its cost of capital and in the top half of the S&P 500.
4. Corporate sales grew 8% year-over-year in Q3, with domestic corporate sales up double digits including mid-teens growth in coastal hubs.
5. Premium revenue grew 9% year-over-year, loyalty revenue improved 9%, and diverse high-margin revenue streams contributed 60% of total revenue.
6. American Express remuneration increased 12% year-over-year to $2 billion in Q3, keeping Delta on track to deliver over $8 billion for the full year.
7. Delta expects full-year 2025 earnings of approximately $6 per share, in the upper half of July guidance, with Q4 earnings guidance of $1.60 to $1.90 per share.
8. Nonfuel unit cost growth was approximately flat year-over-year in Q3, bringing year-to-date nonfuel unit cost growth to less than 2%.
9. Delta paid down nearly $2 billion in debt year-to-date, with gross leverage ending Q3 at 2.4x, and Fitch revised Delta's outlook from stable to positive.
10. Management indicated premium revenue is expected to overtake main cabin revenue in a quarter or two in 2026, with premium products now being the highest-margin products in descending order of premiumness.

1. Neogen delivered Q1 revenue of approximately $209 million, up 0.3% year-over-year on a core basis, which was in line with expectations.
2. The company executed a global headcount reduction of approximately 10% of existing and planned positions, expected to reduce operating expenses by approximately $20 million on an annualized basis.
3. Adjusted EBITDA was $35.5 million in Q1, representing a margin of 17%, down from prior year due to lower volume, gross margin headwinds, and higher operating expenses.
4. Petrifilm, which has had a core revenue CAGR in the mid-single-digit range over recent years, experienced a mid-single-digit decline in Q1 attributed to distributor inventory rebalancing.
5. Q1 free cash flow was an outflow of $13 million, representing an improvement of $43 million compared to the prior year Q1.
6. The company completed the divestiture of its cleaners and disinfectants business for approximately $115 million in net proceeds, using $100 million to pay down debt with annualized interest savings of roughly $6 million.
7. Neogen ended Q1 with gross debt of $800 million (68% at fixed rate) and a total cash position of $139 million.
8. Food Safety segment revenues were $152 million, down 4.6% compared to prior year including a core decline of 1.7%, while Animal Safety segment revenues were $57 million with core revenue growth of 5.8%.
9. The company expects to realize approximately $12 million benefit from cost reduction actions this fiscal year, with more than half already contemplated in initial guidance.
10. Adjusted earnings per share were $0.04 in Q1 compared to $0.07 in the prior year quarter, primarily due to lower adjusted EBITDA which more than offset lower interest expense.

1. Q3 2025 net revenue was $28.2 million, a 35% increase from the $20.9 million reported in Q3 2024.
2. Net income for Q3 2025 was $2.2 million, up from $1 million for Q3 2024.
3. Adjusted EBITDA totaled $3.7 million in Q3 2025, up from $1.9 million for Q3 2024.
4. Gross margin declined to 60% in Q3 2025 from 62% in Q3 2024 due to channel mix shift toward dealer/international sales and start-up costs for the Compact Launcher and Fort Wayne ammo facility.
5. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $9 million at August 31, 2025, down from $25.7 million at November 30, 2024, with the company having no debt.
6. Average daily web sessions on byrna.com increased from 33,000 to over 50,000 following the AI-enabled advertising campaign, reaching 70,000 sessions per day recently.
7. Byrna's opt-in e-mail list has grown to 1.9 million subscribers.
8. The company is now in more than 1,000 retail stores nationwide, with its 5 company-owned stores operating at an average annualized run rate of $725,000 in September.
9. Management expects full year fiscal 2025 revenue growth to be between 35% and 40%.
10. The company targets gross margin percentages of 63% to 65% for next year as manufacturing efficiencies improve.

1. Net sales increased 4.6% to $358.2 million, primarily driven by $24.9 million of inorganic sales from the UW Solutions acquisition.
2. Adjusted diluted EPS declined to $0.98, primarily driven by lower adjusted EBITDA and higher interest expense.
3. The company updated its fiscal 2026 outlook to net sales of $1.39 billion to $1.42 billion and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.60 to $3.90.
4. Services backlog sequentially grew 16% to $792 million, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of year-over-year net sales growth for that segment.
5. Performance Surfaces delivered strong organic growth of 18.6%, primarily from improved retail channel distribution.
6. Net cash provided by operating activities was $57.1 million in Q2, with a consolidated leverage ratio of 1.5x and no near-term debt maturities.
7. Aluminum prices increased approximately 20% on average during Q2, creating cost pressure expected to continue in the second half.
8. The estimated EPS impact from tariffs for fiscal 2026 is $0.35 to $0.45.
9. Metals adjusted EBITDA margin decreased to 14.8%, with margins expected to drop further in Q3 due to higher aluminum costs on longer lead time products.
10. Glass segment is expected to finish the year with mid-teens EBITDA margins despite sales being down significantly year-over-year, compared to mid-single-digit margins during the last downturn.

1. Q3 organic net revenue grew 7%, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of high single-digit organic revenue growth.
2. Global direct-to-consumer sales were up 9% with DTC productivity initiatives resulting in more than 400 basis points of margin expansion in the quarter.
3. E-commerce grew 16% in Q3 driven by increased traffic across all segments, with the company targeting e-commerce to reach 15% of total business up from 9% today.
4. Q3 gross margin reached a record 61.7%, expanding 110 basis points versus prior year while absorbing 80 basis points of tariff headwinds.
5. The company raised full year adjusted diluted EPS guidance by $0.02 to a range of $1.27 to $1.32 and increased organic revenue expectations to approximately 6%.
6. Asia net revenues accelerated to up 12% in Q3, with double-digit growth in key markets like India, Japan, Korea and Turkey.
7. The company returned $151 million to shareholders in Q3, a 118% increase versus last year, and implemented a $120 million accelerated share repurchase program retiring approximately 5 million shares.
8. Levi's Women's business grew 9% in Q3 and 12% year-to-date, while Tops grew 9% in the quarter.
9. Q4 organic net revenue growth is expected to be approximately 1%, with adjusted diluted EPS in the range of $0.36 to $0.38.
10. Updated tariff guidance reflects a full year gross impact of approximately 70 basis points headwind to gross margin before mitigation, with 80 basis points headwind expected in Q4 and $0.03 impact to adjusted diluted EPS.

1. BlackRock achieved record AUM of $13.5 trillion and generated $205 billion of net inflows in Q3, reflecting 10% annualized organic base fee growth—the highest quarter since 2021.
2. Q3 revenue of $6.5 billion increased 25% year-over-year, while operating income of $2.6 billion rose 23% year-over-year.
3. Earnings per share of $11.55 increased only 1% year-over-year due to higher share count from 6.9 million shares issued for GIP and 8.5 million SubCo units issued for HPS.
4. iShares ETFs generated a record $153 billion of net inflows in Q3, with the franchise crossing $5 trillion in total assets.
5. Digital assets ETPs raised $17 billion in Q3, with the flagship IBIT product surpassing $100 billion in AUM.
6. HPS contributed approximately $225 million in base fees and $270 million in performance fees in its first full quarter after closing.
7. The cash management platform crossed $1 trillion in AUM with $34 billion of Q3 net inflows, having grown 45% over the last 3 years.
8. BlackRock's Circle reserve fund mandate surpassed $64 billion, and the tokenized liquidity fund BUIDL has grown to nearly $3 billion in AUM.
9. GIP Fund V closed above its $25 billion target in July, representing the largest ever client capital raise in a private infrastructure fund.
10. As-adjusted operating margin of 44.6% declined 120 basis points year-over-year due to higher performance fees, but excluding performance fees and related compensation, margin expanded 110 basis points to 46.3%.

1. Income from operations increased 11.8% in Q3, excluding the impact of foreign currency.
2. U.S. same-store sales accelerated to 5.2% for the quarter, driven by the Best Deal Ever promotion and Parmesan Stuffed Crust.
3. U.S. carryout comps were up 8.7% while delivery was positive 2.5% for the quarter.
4. Global retail sales grew 6.3% in the quarter, excluding the impact of foreign currency.
5. The company added 29 net new stores in the U.S., bringing the system store count to 7,090.
6. International retail sales grew 5.7% excluding foreign currency, with same-store sales of 1.7% and net store growth of 185.
7. The company refinanced $1 billion in debt at a blended rate of approximately 5.1%, up from the prior blended rate of approximately 4.3%.
8. The company repurchased approximately 166,000 shares at an average price of $450 per share for a total of $75 million in Q3, with approximately $540 million remaining on the share repurchase authorization.
9. Management reiterated expectations for U.S. full-year comp of 3% and operating income growth of approximately 8% excluding foreign currency and one-time items.
10. Management indicated they have seen a slowing across the restaurant industry at the start of the fourth quarter, which could pressure the full year same-store sales outlook.

1. FB Financial reported Q3 2025 EPS of $0.43 and adjusted EPS of $1.07, with adjusted return on average assets of 1.43% and adjusted return on tangible common equity of 14.7%.
2. Net interest margin expanded 27 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 3.95%, benefiting from the Southern States acquisition and approximately $6 million in net accretion from purchase accounting marks.
3. The company achieved organic loan growth of $156 million (approximately 5% annualized) in Q3, with the loan pipeline described as the strongest in about two years.
4. Management expects to achieve 50% of Southern States deal cost synergies in the second half of 2025 and 100% in 2026, earlier than originally modeled.
5. The adjusted core efficiency ratio improved to 53.3% from 56.9% in the prior quarter and 58.4% in the same quarter last year, with expectations to reach approximately 50% by year-end 2026.
6. Net charge-offs were minimal at 5 basis points annualized, with nonperforming assets to total assets declining 3 basis points to 89 basis points.
7. The company executed a deposit remixing strategy that resulted in $392 million of high-cost deposit outflows offset by approximately $320 million in net new relationship deposits.
8. Management guided Q4 and 2026 net interest margin (including accretion) to 3.80%-3.90%, assuming two rate cuts before year-end.
9. Full year 2026 banking expenses are expected to be $325 million to $335 million, excluding potential large investments in revenue producers or market expansion.
10. The company repurchased approximately $24 million of stock during the quarter and paid down $100 million in subordinated debt plus called $30 million in trust preferred securities.

1. JPMorgan Chase reported Q3 2025 net income of $14.4 billion, EPS of $5.07, and ROTCE of 20% on revenue of $47.1 billion, which was up 9% year-on-year.
2. The CIB reported revenue of $19.9 billion, up 17% year-on-year, with Fixed Income up 21% and Equities up 33% from robust client activity.
3. Investment Banking fees were up 16% year-on-year with particular strength in equity underwriting as the IPO market was active, and management stated the pipeline remains robust.
4. Asset & Wealth Management achieved record revenue of $6.1 billion, up 12% year-on-year, with long-term net inflows of $72 billion for the quarter and AUM reaching $4.6 trillion.
5. Management expects 2026 NII excluding Markets to be approximately $95 billion and indicated that the consensus expense estimate of about $100 billion for 2026 looks a little bit low.
6. The 2025 card net charge-off rate expectation was lowered to approximately 3.3% on favorable delinquency trends driven by continued consumer resilience.
7. The CET1 ratio ended the quarter at 14.8%, down 30 basis points versus the prior quarter, primarily driven by increases in wholesale lending across Banking and Markets.
8. Tricolor contributed $170 million of wholesale charge-offs this quarter due to apparent fraud in secured lending facilities, though management confirmed no exposure to First Brands.
9. JPMorgan retained its #1 position in retail deposit share for the fifth consecutive year and reported over 400,000 net new checking accounts this quarter.
10. Management announced an aspiration to add $500 billion of lending to industries critical for U.S. security over the next 10 years, plus $10 billion of incremental direct equity investments.

1. First half fiscal 2026 revenue reached a record $10.3 million, with net income increasing 36% year-over-year to $917,000 ($0.06 per share).
2. The company reported its sixth consecutive quarter of revenue exceeding $5 million, with Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue at $5.16 million.
3. Equipment and service-related backlog stood at $11.2 million at quarter end, near record levels.
4. Medical market sales in Q2 increased 150% year-over-year to $1 million, driven by balloon coating systems shipped to the U.S., Europe, and China.
5. The company announced a $5 million order and a $2.8 million order from major U.S. medical device manufacturers in recent weeks.
6. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $10.6 million with no outstanding debt as of August 31, 2025.
7. Gross profit margin improved to 50-51% from 49% in the prior year period due to favorable product mix of mature high ASP systems.
8. Asia sales increased 153% year-over-year in Q2 ($562,000), while U.S./Canada sales decreased 22% ($775,000) due to slowing clean energy momentum.
9. Operating income for the first half increased 73% to $905,000, with operating margin improving to 9% from 5% in the prior year.
10. The company raised full-year guidance to reflect modest revenue growth, expecting medical device demand to offset anticipated declines in clean energy orders.

1. Goldman Sachs generated Q3 2025 net revenues of $15.2 billion, earnings per share of $12.25, and an ROE of 14.2%.
2. The firm advised on over $1 trillion in announced M&A volumes for 2025 year-to-date, $220 billion ahead of its next closest competitor.
3. Advisory revenues of $1.4 billion were up 60% versus a year ago, reflecting a significant increase in completed transactions.
4. Assets under supervision rose to a record $3.5 trillion, with the 31st consecutive quarter of long-term fee-based net inflows.
5. The firm raised a record $33 billion in alternatives in the quarter and now expects to raise approximately $100 billion in alternatives for the full year, substantially exceeding prior expectations.
6. Total financing revenues of $2.8 billion rose 23% year-over-year and now comprise nearly 40% of overall FICC and Equities revenues.
7. Quarter-end investment banking backlog reached its highest level in 3 years despite very strong accruals.
8. Sponsor activity is tracking 40% higher versus last year, with sponsors holding over $1 trillion in dry powder and $4 trillion in private equity portfolio assets.
9. The company returned $3.3 billion to shareholders in Q3, including $1.3 billion in common stock dividends and $2 billion in share repurchases.
10. Management and other fees rose 12% year-over-year to a record $2.9 billion, while the year-to-date compensation ratio improved by 100 basis points to 32.5%.

1. Citigroup reported Q3 2025 adjusted EPS of $2.24 and adjusted ROTCE of 9.7%, excluding a $726 million goodwill impairment related to Banamex.
2. Total revenues increased 9% year-over-year, with all five business segments achieving record Q3 revenue and positive operating leverage.
3. Share repurchases totaled $5 billion in Q3, $1 billion above prior guidance, bringing year-to-date buybacks to $8.75 billion of a $20 billion program.
4. Markets revenues grew 15% with prime balances up approximately 44% and equities revenues increasing 24%.
5. Wealth segment recorded $18.6 billion in net new investment assets in Q3, with over $52 billion in the last 12 months representing approximately 9% organic growth.
6. CET1 capital ratio ended at 13.2%, with management targeting 12.8% going forward based on a reduced stress capital buffer (from 4.1% to 3.6%) and a 100 basis point management buffer.
7. Citigroup announced an agreement for Fernando Chico Pardo to purchase a 25% equity stake in Banamex at a fixed 0.8x book value multiple, with regulatory approval expected to take 9 to 12 months.
8. Management is targeting an ROTCE of 10% to 11% for 2026 and an efficiency ratio below 60% exiting 2026.
9. Transformation expenses are expected to be slightly under $3.5 billion in 2025 and are projected to decline in 2026 as programs are completed.
10. Full year 2025 revenues are expected to exceed $84 billion, with NII ex-markets projected to increase approximately 5.5% for the year.

1. Q3 2025 EPS was $1.05, up $0.13 or 14% sequentially, with PPNR up 9% sequentially and 20% year-over-year.
2. Net interest margin expanded 5 basis points to 3.00%, with medium-term target maintained at 3.25% to 3.50%.
3. Private Bank deposits grew $3.8 billion to $12.5 billion in Q3, already exceeding the year-end target of $12 billion.
4. Capital Markets delivered a record third quarter and second-best quarterly performance ever, with strong results across M&A, debt underwriting, loan syndication, and equity underwriting.
5. The Private Bank achieved cumulative breakeven in approximately 2 years, contributing $0.08 to EPS this quarter versus $0.06 in the prior quarter.
6. The Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.46, a $0.04 or 9.5% increase, with $75 million in share repurchases executed during the quarter.
7. Net charge-offs declined to 46 basis points from 48 basis points in the prior quarter, with Q4 guidance for charge-offs in the low 40s basis points.
8. The Reimagine the Bank initiative is expected to deliver fully phased-in run rate benefits greater than $400 million, with net benefits beginning in 2027 and accelerating into 2028.
9. General office portfolio balance of $2.5 billion has declined approximately 40% or $1.6 billion since March 2023, with a reserve coverage of 12.4%.
10. Q4 2025 guidance includes NII up approximately 2.5% to 3%, NIM expansion of approximately 5 basis points, and share repurchases of roughly $125 million.

1. Adjusted earnings per share increased $0.06 from the prior quarter to $0.51, driving adjusted return on tangible common equity up 135 basis points to 15%.
2. Net interest income grew $33 million with net interest margin expanding 15 basis points to 3.55%, though management indicated the high 3.30s to low 3.40s is a better baseline excluding one-time Main Street Lending Program accretion.
3. Share buybacks accelerated to $190 million with approximately 8.6 million shares repurchased, and more than $300 million remains in buyback authorization.
4. The company retained approximately 97% of the $29 billion in deposit balances associated with clients who had a repricing event in the quarter while continuing to reduce costs on those deposits.
5. CET1 ratio remained flat at 11%, with management announcing a near-term target of 10.75% and a longer-term normalized target of 10% to 10.5%.
6. Net charge-offs decreased by $7 million to $26 million, resulting in a net charge-off ratio of 17 basis points, at the low end of the 15-25 basis point full-year guidance.
7. C&I portfolio period-end balances grew $174 million quarter-over-quarter, while loans to mortgage companies decreased $132 million due to normal seasonality.
8. Criticized and classified loans declined approximately 9%, or $330 million, in the quarter, contributing to a decline in the ACL-to-loans ratio to 1.38%.
9. The third quarter was the company's highest origination funding quarter in the last two years, with management expressing confidence in mid-single-digit loan growth for 2026.
10. Adjusted expenses increased $45 million from the prior quarter, including a $20 million contribution to the First Horizon Foundation to maximize tax advantages available in 2025.

1. PNC reported Q3 2025 net income of $1.8 billion, or $4.35 per diluted share, with year-to-date diluted EPS growth of 17% compared to the same period last year.
2. The net charge-off ratio was only 22 basis points, with net loan charge-offs of $179 million declining $19 million from the prior quarter.
3. Total revenue reached a record $5.9 billion, up $254 million or 4% linked quarter, with over 200 basis points of positive operating leverage.
4. Average loans grew to $326 billion, up $3 billion or 1%, with commercial loans increasing $3.4 billion or 2% while commercial real estate declined $1 billion or 3%.
5. Average deposits increased $9 billion or 2% to $432 billion, driven by 7% growth in commercial interest-bearing deposits.
6. Capital Markets and Advisory revenue increased $111 million or 35% linked quarter, driven by increased M&A advisory activity and higher underwriting and loan syndication revenue.
7. The CET1 ratio was 10.6%, with CET1 inclusive of AOCI at 9.7%, and the company returned $1 billion to shareholders including $679 million in dividends and $331 million in share repurchases.
8. Management expects full-year 2025 NII growth of 6.5% and confirmed 2026 NII growth will be 'comfortably' above $1 billion on top of 2025 levels.
9. Net interest margin was 2.79%, down 1 basis point due to outsized commercial deposit growth, but management expects NIM to exceed 3% during 2026.
10. The company announced the acquisition of FirstBank, which will make PNC the #1 market share position in retail deposits in Denver and more than triple its Colorado branch footprint.

1. EPS was $1.06, up 31% year-over-year, while revenue reached $28 billion, up 11% year-over-year.
2. Return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) improved to 15.4% in the quarter.
3. Net interest income on a fully taxable equivalent basis reached a record $15.4 billion, up 9% year-over-year.
4. Investment banking fees exceeded $2 billion, up 43% year-over-year, with advisory up 51%, debt underwriting up 42%, and equity underwriting up 34%.
5. The company returned $7.4 billion to shareholders through $2.1 billion in common dividends and $5.3 billion in share repurchases.
6. Fourth quarter NII is expected to be at the higher end of the $15.5-$15.7 billion range ($15.6 billion or higher on FTE basis), representing approximately 8% growth from Q4 2024.
7. Full year 2026 NII growth is expected to be 5% to 7%, driven by loan and deposit growth plus fixed rate asset repricing at 150 to 200 basis points higher yields.
8. Net charge-offs declined 10% from Q2 to $1.4 billion, with the total net charge-off ratio falling to 47 basis points, down 8 basis points from Q2.
9. Consumer Banking delivered $3.4 billion in net income, up 28% year-over-year, with over 600 basis points of operating leverage and an efficiency ratio below 50%.
10. CET1 ratio increased to 11.6%, well above the 10% regulatory minimum, with tangible book value per share rising 8% year-over-year to $28.39.

1. Abbott reported organic sales growth of 7.5% excluding COVID test sales, with adjusted earnings per share of $1.30, up high single digits year-over-year.
2. Medical Devices sales grew 12.5%, driven by double-digit growth in Diabetes Care, Electrophysiology, Cardiac Rhythm Management, Heart Failure, and Structural Heart.
3. Continuous glucose monitor sales reached $2 billion in the quarter, representing 17% growth.
4. Recently launched new products generated nearly $500 million in sales this quarter, adding more than 100 basis points to organic sales growth.
5. Adjusted gross margin was 55.8% of sales, reflecting a decrease compared to prior year due to tariff impacts, while adjusted operating margin increased 40 basis points year-over-year to 23%.
6. Core Lab Diagnostics grew 7% excluding China, with the U.S. showing acceleration to 10% growth in Q3 driven by new business capture.
7. The Cardiac Rhythm Management business has outperformed the market for 10 consecutive quarters, with growth accelerating from high single digits last year to double digits this quarter.
8. Management expressed comfort with 2026 consensus estimates of 7.5% organic sales growth and 10% EPS growth, citing pipeline momentum and easing headwinds.
9. China now represents less than 6% of total Abbott revenue, down from approximately 9-10% ten years ago, with mid-single-digit growth expected for 2026 excluding diagnostics headwinds.
10. Abbott plans to initiate pivotal trials next year for mitral valve replacement, balloon TAVR, AVEIR conduction system pacing, peripheral IVL, and continuous lactate monitor sensor, with close to 200 clinical trials planned across all businesses.

1. Morgan Stanley generated record revenues of $18.2 billion and EPS of $2.80 in Q3 2025, with a return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) of 23.5%.
2. Total client assets across Wealth and Investment Management reached $8.9 trillion, up $1.3 trillion over the last year.
3. Wealth Management delivered record revenues of $8.2 billion with a reported pretax margin of 30.3%, adding $81 billion in net new assets and $42 billion in fee-based flows.
4. Investment Banking revenues increased to $2.1 billion, with underwriting results up over 50% year-over-year, marking one of the strongest quarters in recent years.
5. Equity underwriting revenues increased 80% year-over-year to $652 million, driven by IPO activity and strength across equity products and sectors.
6. The equities business generated $4.1 billion in revenue, with prime brokerage average client balances and financing revenues reaching new records.
7. The firm's standardized CET1 ratio stands at 15.2%, with excess CET1 capital of over 300 basis points, and the company repurchased $1.1 billion of common stock in the quarter.
8. Investment Management reached record total AUM of $1.8 trillion with long-term net inflows of $16.5 billion, over half driven by Parametric.
9. Bank lending balances in Wealth Management rose $5 billion sequentially to $174 billion, while total end-period deposits grew to $398 billion.
10. Management expects a modest sequential gain in net interest income in Q4 2025 and sees potential for NII inflection higher despite Fed rate cuts due to continued lending balance growth.

1. Management expects high single-digit year-over-year loan growth as the target for the full year.
2. Core net interest margin ended Q3 at 4.55% and is expected to compress to approximately 4.50% with the first Q4 rate cut and potentially to 4.47% with additional rate cuts.
3. New loan fundings are pricing between 7.00% and 7.25%, slightly below the September average of 7.4%.
4. Loan fee income now represents approximately 40 basis points of the net interest margin.
5. Management guided core fee income to approximately $1 million and noninterest expense to $9 million to $9.5 million for Q4.
6. The mortgage pipeline has increased to approximately 3x the number of transactions and dollar volume expected to close in the next 60 days compared to 6 months ago.
7. Credit migrations during the quarter were described as very benign and slightly positive overall.
8. Management increased the loan loss reserve due to portfolio growth and increased volatility in macro credit conditions.
9. Competitive pressure is currently more pronounced on the deposit side than on the loan side.
10. The company's controlling shareholders own more than 50% of the shares, which management says influences their disciplined approach to M&A.

1. Banner Corporation reported Q3 2025 EPS of $1.54, compared to $1.30 in Q3 2024 and $1.31 in Q2 2025.
2. Core pretax pre-provision earnings increased 18% year-over-year to $67.8 million in Q3 2025, up from $57.4 million in Q3 2024.
3. Tax equivalent net interest margin was 3.98% for Q3 2025, up 6 basis points from 3.92% in the prior quarter.
4. Core deposits represent 89% of total deposits, with loans and core deposits both increasing 4% year-over-year.
5. Banner increased its quarterly dividend by 4% to $0.50 per common share and repurchased 250,000 shares at an average price of $63.50 during the quarter.
6. Deposits increased by $489 million during the quarter, allowing the company to pay down $459 million in FHLB advances.
7. Adversely classified loans declined by $16 million quarter-over-quarter to 1.49% of total loans, while nonperforming assets represent just 0.27% of total assets.
8. Tangible common equity ratio stands at 9.5%, with tangible common equity per share increasing 9% year-over-year.
9. Average rate on new loan production was 7.35% in Q3 2025, compared to 7.27% in the prior quarter, with 29% of the loan portfolio being adjustable rate.
10. Management expects mid-single-digit loan growth for the full year 2025 and anticipates moderate margin compression in Q4 if multiple Fed rate cuts occur as forecasted.

1. The company cut 5% of its expense base, with the majority of those savings commencing in Q4 2025.
2. Q4 2025 expenses are expected to be $96.5 million, with the same level or better targeted for Q4 2026.
3. The company targets 20% annual growth in transportation revenue.
4. Q3 2025 annualized transportation revenue was $240 million, implying roughly $50 million of targeted growth in 2026.
5. Excluding LoadPay investments, the payments segment EBITDA margin would be almost 30%.
6. LoadPay account openings doubled over the prior quarter, with approximately 70% of accounts getting linked quickly after opening.
7. A linked and funded LoadPay account generates $750 in annual revenue, with some accounts reaching $4,000-$5,000 annually due to debit card interchange fees.
8. The company invested $110 million in technology on its cost base this quarter.
9. TriumphPay touches 47% of all invoices from a payments perspective and 64% when combining audit and payments.
10. The company identified a $42 million high-margin revenue infill opportunity from increasing pricing for existing TriumphPay customers to full rates.

1. United delivered Q3 2025 EPS of $2.78, exceeding the top end of its guidance range of $2.25 to $2.75 and Wall Street expectations of $2.68.
2. The company expects Q4 2025 EPS of $3.00 to $3.50, positioning full-year EPS toward the better half of its $9 to $11 guidance range.

1. Design Therapeutics expects to report data from the RESTORE-FA Phase 1b multiple ascending dose trial of DT-216 in Friedreich Ataxia patients in the second half of 2026.
2. Cellular data suggest that 10 nanomolar drug levels may be sufficient to fully increase frataxin mRNA and protein in patient-derived iPSC neurons, given sufficient duration of exposure.
3. Prior 2023 clinical data showed plasma exposures of ~40–75 nM at day 2 corresponded to ~8–10 nM in muscle and produced an unmistakable increase in frataxin RNA expression, which dropped off after day 2 as drug cleared.
4. The current drug product DT-216P2 at ~40 mg delivered sustained 40–75 nM plasma levels through one week in single-dose PK, supporting weekly dosing with build-up to higher steady-state with multiple doses.
5. RESTORE-FA escalates IV dosing from 0.1 to 0.3 to 0.6 to 1 mg/kg over 4-week cohorts, with 12-week treatment cohorts including the 1 mg/kg group added to enable the 2H 2026 readout, and PK projections support additional dose levels within nonclinical safety exposures.
6. Subcutaneous infusion dosing details remain to be determined, with the company prioritizing IV (fully bioavailable) first to set dose levels before subcu cohorts.
7. The trial will measure four frataxin biomarkers (mRNA and protein in both blood and muscle) and report change from baseline, with blood mRNA showing the least overlap between patient and carrier levels making it best-suited to assess carrier-range responses.
8. Management identified three biomarker scorecard questions for the readout: whether DT-216 increases frataxin mRNA in either tissue, increases frataxin protein in blood or muscle, and shows activity in both blood and muscle.
9. Clinical exploratory endpoints include mFARS, the Upright Stability Score subcomponent (used as primary in the approved drug's BRAVE study), and the PROMIS Fatigue Scale (3-point MIC).
10. Management cited mFARS benchmarks of ~2.4-point treated-vs-placebo difference (1.56-point change from baseline) for omaveloxolone in MOXIe at 48 weeks, Lexeo's reported 2-point improvement at 6 months (n=16), and Larimar's 2.25-point improvement at 1 year (n=8) as context for interpreting any clinical trends in RESTORE-FA.

1. AXPAXLI achieved superiority over aflibercept in the SOL-1 Phase III wet AMD trial with a p-value of 0.0006 on the primary endpoint, marking the first time a novel investigational therapy demonstrated superiority to an approved anti-VEGF in a Phase III wet AMD trial.
2. In SOL-1, approximately 75% of patients maintained vision at 9 months and 66% maintained vision through 12 months with just a single AXPAXLI injection, despite enrolling a best-seeing wet AMD population intentionally selected to lose vision.
3. The rescue rate observed in the aflibercept arm at week 28 was not reached in the AXPAXLI arm until week 52, representing a roughly 6-month delay in clinically meaningful disease change.
4. Subjects treated with AXPAXLI took 5 to 6 months longer than aflibercept-treated subjects to reach fluid volume increase thresholds of >30 and >75 microns from week 8.
5. No treatment-related serious ocular or systemic adverse events such as endophthalmitis or vasculitis were observed in SOL-1, supporting a reassuring safety profile.
6. Ocular remains on track to submit an NDA for AXPAXLI in wet AMD based on SOL-1 week 52 data using the 505(b)(2) pathway, subject to ongoing formal FDA discussions, with the FDA's single registrational trial framework expected to phase in over the coming months.
7. SOL-R completed randomization of 631 subjects in December 2025, exceeding the original 555-subject target, enabling acceleration of top-line data guidance to Q1 2027.
8. The company initiated enrollment in SOL-X, a 3-year open-label extension allowing SOL-1 and SOL-R completers to receive AXPAXLI for a total of 5 years follow-up, with crossover patients providing data on consequences of delaying AXPAXLI treatment.
9. Ocular ended Q1 2026 with approximately $667 million in cash, providing runway into 2028, though this does not include full anticipated commercialization expenses for AXPAXLI.
10. In SOL-1, using SOL-R rescue criteria nearly 80% of patients were rescue-free at 6 months and 56% maintained stable central subfield thickness within 30 microns after a single injection, supporting confidence in SOL-R's non-inferiority readout.

9. 8. ENTR-601-44 targets approximately 8% of the global DMD patient population (exon 44 skip-amenable mutations) and received FDA Rare Pediatric Disease designation in December.
9. Management guided that ELEVATE-45-201 Cohort 1 (5 mg/kg) is likely to show lower-than-expected exon skipping and dystrophin due to similar PK assumptions, but still expects potential functional improvement, with the competitive bar for exon 45 dystrophin at ~1%.

9. Backlog incentive rate going into Q3 stands at approximately 12.5% versus 12.9% in Q2, suggesting only modest further sequential improvement in incentive levels.
